title: My agent-ported UE 5.9 voxel game hitched for two reasons: a Rust function the port skipped (up to 68 ms) and a texture nothing read (about half of a 152 ms first spawn)
author: VictorBuildsApps
selftext:
Irismere is my unreleased voxel action-adventure, built with coding agents. It started in Rust, and since 9 November the agents have been porting it to Unreal 5.9. Once creatures ran in normal play, the game hitched. In one staged run (a save copy set to 21:50, a scripted bot, one placed creature), 18 creature updates took over 8 ms and the worst took 152.6 ms. The night test had passed both times it ran. It only logged its worst step, 73 ms, without saying where it came from.

A CPU trace of the real game showed which updates were slow (-csvNamedEventsTiming puts the existing CSV stat in Unreal Insights without a rebuild). For the pathfinding updates it had nothing underneath, so the agents sampled the main thread's call stack in a separate run without a renderer, and that pointed at the section reads. Timing the look build on its own showed the second cause.

1. Pathfinding. The Rust version reads a whole stored section of blocks at a time for creature routes. Its comment says reading block by block costs about 7 ms a section. The port never brought that function over, so every section the planner needed was 36,864 single block and fluid lookups, about 2.8 ms in a standalone build. Reading whole sections takes 86 microseconds. A test compares the cells from the old and new reads, 23.9 million of them, and none differ.

2. First sight of a species. About a second after load-in, the first population check showed 47 creatures at once and built each new species' look in that update. In a standalone benchmark, 97% of that build was filling a preview texture that no creature code reads. It's gone now, and the atlas, palette, parts and meshes of all 33 looks hash the same before and after.

Same staged save and same bot input after both fixes: updates over 8 ms went from 18 to 1, the worst from 152.6 to 50.6 ms (127.3 ms after the first fix), and frames over 33 ms with one of those updates inside from 6 to 1. The 50 ms left is that same first check: it still creates all its components in one update, and registering the new textures is 8 ms of it. One run per build, in the editor with a trace running, not a packaged build.

For the pathfinding, the behaviour checks were right and the speed path was missing. The original even had a comment saying why it existed. If you've had agents port code between languages, did they drop things like this, and how did you catch them?
